brief:
Goal: recover each whole function so a dedicated server for the original 12.60 client can run battle royale (lobby to bus to storm to win). Go as deep as it takes: follow callees, identify and name helpers, members and virtual slots, recover and propose dependencies yourself, and keep going until each function has a complete, faithful body. Hints from the earlier inventory (porting/server_authority_inventory.md, partial, may be wrong): These are the listed entry points, but the real task is to find and recover the server logic that is not yet located: who writes AFortPlayerStateAthena Kills/Downs/DeathInfo, how a player or team is eliminated (damage to death, DBNO, ServerCreateAthenaDeathInfo style flow, spectating), how the win condition is detected and WinningTeam/WinningPlayerState/GamePhase end-of-match are written on AFortGameStateAthena, and how a player joins and spawns in the pre-match lobby island and aircraft. Use the reflection (replicated property offsets), field-offset queries and call graph to attribute the writers, then recover those functions (including non-reflected ones) as dependencies.

How to work: you have a large budget; use it. Do not stop at the first unnamed callee, unreflected member, virtual slot, timer or config value: open the decompile, read the callee, recover it, write it as a dependency (helper, member or virtual declaration under work/dependencies/) and carry on until the whole function body is written. Each function is finished only when its full body is written, and a function that calls helpers is finished by writing the helpers too. Do not end your run while any listed function lacks a body; if one is hard, work on it longer rather than moving on, and make the most faithful source-level choice the evidence supports, noting residual uncertainty in the evidence file as a CONFIDENCE comment. Record every function as proposed once it has a body. A previous pass on related functions left partial evidence and dependency drafts in work/ and work/dependencies/; reuse them.
